title: A little reflecting ahead of tonight’s festivities!!! #ImmersivePhant...
transcript: The craziest part about the immersive Phantom Masquerade giveaway is that I almost didn't make it. If you follow me on other platforms, you may already know this, but I was actually in Baltimore yesterday afternoon, and we were actually driving back and had just gotten to Brooklyn when I got the notification that they were doing another drop. So obviously, I had to drop everything and go. Our initial plan was to head back to my friend's apartment to watch K pop demon hunters, but instead, I said, can you just let me off here? And I got out of the car and went to the nearest subway station to head up to Midtown as fast as I possibly could. And even still, I got in there like, an hour after they started the giveaway. And so, like, if we had left an hour later or had hit more traffic, I would not have made it, and I would not be seeing the opening night of masquerade tonight. All this to say, I've seen some speculation online of, like, was it rigged for me to win? And, well, obviously, I will never know what went on behind the scenes. I can tell you that if they wanted to give me tickets to their opening night, there were a million other easier and less risky ways for them to do that. They have my contact info. They could have dmed me on any number of social media platforms. And so While I obviously can't say 100% that it wasn't rigged, I do think it doesn't really make logical sense for them to do that. And there is a part of this that does kind of feel like fate. I had made my peace with not being able to go to opening weeks ago, so a lot of things had to go right for me. Not only did I have to win, but I also had to not have anything planned tonight. I have anything planned last night during the giveaway, had to get back from Baltimore just in time. And I am such a believer that what is meant for you will not pass you by. And I do feel like this was the universe's way of telling me this is meant for you. Go have fun and enjoy the culmination of a month long journey with the show. And so, regardless of how I got that winning ticket, whether it was fate or whether it was rigged, I still feel so incredibly lucky to be attending this opening. And I cannot wait to celebrate with all of the cast and crew that made this incredible achievement possible.
classificationReason: Opus reclassified: has opinion — I had to drop everything and go
reasoning: This transcript is about winning tickets to opening night of 'Masquerade' (Phantom sequel) and discusses the giveaway process and anticipation for attending the show. The creator uses future tense ('I cannot wait to celebrate') and hasn't actually seen the show yet - this is pre-show excitement content, not a review.
